highlights: A courtesy call the day before every delivery or collection
Allergen card and menu included with every platter
Complimentary crackers with all cheese-based platters
Vegan cheese platters and gluten-free crackers on the menu
Hand-delivery Tuesday to Saturday, with timed windows available
10% off every fifth order for registered customers

howItWorks.title: Browse online
howItWorks.text: Everything they offer is listed on their website, with full prices shown.

howItWorks.title: Build your basket
howItWorks.text: Add products to the basket, along with any notes and allergy or dietary requirements. A £130 minimum spend applies for hand-delivery within the M25 and Essex.

howItWorks.title: Choose delivery or collection
howItWorks.text: Standard delivery is added at checkout, or you can add a timed delivery slot. Collection from their Romford HQ can be selected instead.

howItWorks.title: Check out and confirm
howItWorks.text: Add your date and address, agree to the terms and check out. An order confirmation email follows, and it is worth checking the products, date, slot and dietary details carefully.

howItWorks.title: Confirmation call
howItWorks.text: The day before your delivery or collection, the team calls to confirm all the details, and they follow up afterwards to check everything was perfect.

howItWorks.title: Delivery
howItWorks.text: Once your order is packed at HQ, an email confirms it is on its way, and their own courier hand-delivers it within your booked slot.

goodToKnow.text: Local delivery runs Tuesday to Saturday. Standard delivery (8am–5pm) is £15; a morning window (8am–12pm) is standard delivery plus £25, an afternoon window (12pm–4pm) is standard delivery plus £5, and a chosen two-hour window between 6am and 4pm is standard delivery plus £55 or £60, depending on the window.

Deliveries are made strictly to the ground floor (front door, concierge or building reception) or to a loading bay, which must be pre-booked if the building requires it. If there is nowhere safe and legal to unload outside, someone needs to meet the courier.

The person who placed the order should be there to receive it and check everything on arrival. Missing, incorrect or damaged items must be reported at the point of delivery, with photos, before the order is accepted.
Delivery details can be changed within a two-hour grace period after booking; after that, the delivery window and address cannot be changed.

If no one is available and there is no safe place to leave the order, the courier waits up to 10 minutes; re-delivery, where possible, costs £25. Any parking charges the courier has to pay are passed on to the customer.

Ready-to-eat food is freshly prepared on the day of delivery or collection and is best enjoyed that day. Platters are delicate, must be kept perfectly flat, and anything that needs chilling should go straight into the fridge.
UK shipping needs a £50 minimum spend.

Overnight UK shipping, usually by DHL, is available for selected products and arrives Tuesday to Thursday between 8am and 8pm (later in busy periods). The chilled packaging keeps items food-safe for at least 24 hours.

faqs.q: How far in advance should we order?
faqs.a: As early as possible. They need only 48 hours' notice for last-minute orders, but some days close once they reach capacity, so ordering ahead avoids disappointment.

Most of the M25 area and Essex. The full postcode list is on their Delivery Policy page, and you can also check your postcode at checkout. If you are just outside the area, they may be able to help depending on availability, or you can arrange your own courier to collect from their HQ.

faqs.q: Can we collect the order ourselves?
faqs.a: Yes. Choose collection at checkout; collections from the Romford HQ run Tuesday to Saturday, 9am–10am, and must be made within the booked slot.

faqs.q: Can we add items after ordering?
faqs.a: They will always try to fit in last-minute additions, depending on availability, so get in touch as soon as possible. Pantry, drinks and serveware items can also be added to an existing order.

faqs.q: Should the platter stay in its box?
faqs.a: Either works. Each platter is arranged on a wooden board that can be lifted out to serve, or it can be kept in its branded box. Several platters lined up together give a grazing-table effect.

faqs.q: How should cheese platters be served?
faqs.a: Store them cold but do not serve them cold: take them out of the fridge one to two hours before serving for the best flavour.

faqs.q: How are allergies and dietary needs handled?
faqs.a: Add any allergy or dietary requirements at the basket stage. Every platter comes with an allergy notice card and a menu listing the relevant allergens.

serviceDetails.name: Sharing & grazing platters
serviceDetails.more: Pre-cut versions are available: the Pre-Cut British Cheese & Charcuterie Platter is listed with 150 bites and the Pre-Cut British Cheese Platter with 175. Platters arrive in branded boxes, and complimentary crackers come with every cheese-based platter.

serviceDetails.name: Grazing table styling kits
serviceDetails.more: They pitch the kits as a way to get the look of a styled grazing table without paying styling fees or hiring equipment: unpack the kit, follow the guide and arrange the platters. The four sizes cover anything from cosy gatherings to big celebrations.

serviceDetails.name: PR mailers & brand activations
serviceDetails.more: Past projects shown on their website include press and influencer brunch boxes for beauty launches, DIY grazing and cheese kits, festive hampers, cheese workshops and a Parisian-style pop-up market stall.

serviceDetails.name: Breakfast, brunch & lunch catering
serviceDetails.more: The range includes croissant and pastry, Danish pastry and pastel de nata platters, a vegan banana bread and nut butter platter, and demi-brioche bun and mini bagel platters with a choice of fillings. The Croissant & Pastry Platter is listed at 24 portions, and build-your-own brunch and lunch boxes are also offered.
